title: Semiconductor risks: the map is changing
deck: The chip supply chain is diversifying, but concentration is not disappearing. It is moving into new bottlenecks.
author: NEXUS Industry Desk
takeaway: More fabs do not automatically mean more resilience. Advanced packaging, power, and tooling remain highly concentrated.

sections.title: Resilience has a cost
sections.body: Redundant capacity is not free capacity. Regional incentives are accelerating construction, while utilization and labor pools remain geographically uneven.

sections.title: The Taiwan variable
sections.body: Geopolitical concentration is the most visible risk, but the practical shock channels are operational: lead times, packaging, shipping insurance, and customer allocation.

sections.title: Signals before the headline
sections.body: Watch equipment orders, substrate inventories, and foundry lead times before relying on end-market revenue. These indicators move earlier in the cycle.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.summary: Capacity arrives in sequence and AI demand absorbs the incremental wafer supply.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.summary: Leading-edge remains tight while mature nodes normalize gradually.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.summary: A policy or geopolitical shock overwhelms buffer inventory.
